title: No __main__ guard: entire script runs at import time
description: The file has no `if __name__ == "__main__"` and no main(); all work is module-level. Importing it instantiates the model (38), calls torch.load on a checkpoint (45), builds full N-MNIST + SHD test loaders and densifies the entire SHD test set into a list (54-77), runs the transfer eval (81), and writes a results CSV (120-123) as pure import side effects. Unlike m7_trimodal_run it does not launch training, so no 4-5h run, but it does perform a checkpoint load, dataset build, and a (fabricated) CSV write purely on import. Any static tool or downstream module that imports it triggers all of this.
evidence: No occurrence of `__main__` or `def main` in the file (grep count 0). Module-level statements at lines 37-127.
fix: Wrap lines 37-127 in `def main():` and gate with `if __name__ == "__main__": main()`, mirroring eval_transfer_fixed.py.

title: Fabricated accuracy/forgetting literals written to a results CSV (RULE 1)
description: The CSV row mixes LIVE-computed transfer metrics (v2a/a2v/prototype_alignment/sil_visual, 113-116) with HARDCODED accuracy and forgetting literals: T1_after_T1=97.50, T2_after_T2=72.26, T3_after_T3=76.89, T1_after_T2=95.81, T1_after_T3=95.65, T2_after_T3=73.14 (106-107), and forgetting fields computed from those literals (108-112). These accuracies have no CSV/checkpoint provenance in-repo and are written into results/cl_rehearsal/cl_rehearsal_results.csv with identical formatting to the measured columns, so a downstream reader cannot tell fabricated from measured. Direct RULE-1 violation. The literals also match none of the C_frozen/C_unfrozen/A_no_align columns hardcoded in run_cl_rehearsal.py (435-444), i.e. yet another distinct unsourced set.
evidence: Lines 106-112 assign float literals to accuracy/forgetting keys; lines 108-112 derive forgetting as arithmetic on those literals (e.g. `97.50 - 95.81`).
fix: Do not write hardcoded accuracies. Either compute T1/T2/T3 test accuracy and forgetting live from the loaded checkpoint(s) exactly as run_cl_rehearsal.run_rehearsal_cell does, or drop those columns entirely and write only the live transfer metrics. Never persist a literal as if it were measured.

title: CSV replay_weight=1.0 contradicts reconstructed config (use_replay=False, replay_weight=0.3)
description: The written row sets replay_weight=1.0 (117), but the reconstructed cfg has use_replay=False and replay_weight=0.3 (31). The value 1.0 appears to be the run_cl_rehearsal raw_replay_weight (a different knob feeding RawInputReplayBuffer), not cfg.replay_weight. Writing 1.0 under the column name `replay_weight` mislabels the provenance of the row and is internally inconsistent with the cfg the same file reconstructs.
evidence: Line 117 `"replay_weight": 1.0,` vs line 31 `use_replay=False, ..., replay_weight=0.3`.
fix: Record the actual knob that governed the run under an unambiguous name (e.g. raw_replay_weight) and, if replay_weight is reported, take it from cfg.replay_weight. Reconcile against run_cl_rehearsal.py's actual raw_replay_weight=1.0 vs cfg.replay_weight=0.3 distinction.

title: torch.load of a non-existent checkpoint crashes the module on import
description: Loads results/cl_rehearsal/checkpoints/C_rehearsal_seed42/final_dvs_dvs.pt (43-45). results/ does not exist in the repo (confirmed: results/cl_rehearsal MISSING), so torch.load raises FileNotFoundError. Combined with the missing __main__ guard (CLE-001), merely importing this module raises today. The map_location=str(device) and the assumption the checkpoint is a dict with key 'model_state_dict' add further fragility.
evidence: Line 44-45 build ckpt_t3 and call `torch.load(ckpt_t3, ...)["model_state_dict"]`; results/cl_rehearsal does not exist on disk.
fix: After adding the main guard (CLE-001), check `ckpt_t3.exists()` and exit with a clear message if absent; validate the loaded object has 'model_state_dict'.

title: cfg is a hand-copied duplicate of run_cl_rehearsal.py's config (drift hazard)
description: The ExperimentConfig block (22-35) is a manual copy of the config in run_cl_rehearsal.py, flagged by its own comment `# --- Reconstruct config (must match run_cl_rehearsal.py) ---` (21). A hand-maintained 'must match' duplicate is a classic drift hazard, and it has already drifted in effect (see the replay_weight discrepancy, CLE-003). If the source config changes, this eval silently evaluates under a different config than the run that produced the checkpoint.
evidence: Line 21 comment plus the literal block 22-35, which mirrors run_cl_rehearsal.py:377-390.
fix: Load the config that was saved alongside the checkpoint (the run writes config_*.json / master_config.json) via ExperimentConfig(**json.load(...)) rather than re-declaring it, as eval_transfer_fixed.py and phase1_sanity_check.py already do.

title: CSV column 'silhouette_score' stores only the visual silhouette
description: The column named silhouette_score is assigned transfer_metrics['sil_visual'] only (116); sil_audio is computed by the transfer eval but silently dropped. The generic column name implies a single/combined silhouette, obscuring that it is visual-only.
evidence: Line 116 `"silhouette_score": transfer_metrics["sil_visual"],`; the eval also returns sil_audio (printed at 89 but not persisted).
fix: Rename the column sil_visual and add a sil_audio column, matching the schema eval_transfer_fixed.py uses.

title: Unused imports and dead objects (random_split, dvs_collate_fn, trainer, buffer)
description: random_split (51) and dvs_collate_fn (17) are imported but never used. `buffer` (39) and `trainer` (40) are constructed but never used again -- only `model` is used for the transfer eval -- so both are dead objects (buffer exists solely to feed the unused trainer). These add import-time work and imply capabilities the script does not exercise.
evidence: grep: random_split count 1 (import only), dvs_collate_fn count 1 (import only); trainer referenced once (its assignment, line 40); buffer referenced twice (assignment 39 + passed to the unused trainer 40).
fix: Remove the unused imports and the buffer/trainer construction.

title: Missing config_nmnist.json crashes main() on the normal path
description: main() opens CKPT_DIR/config_nmnist.json with no existence check (61-62). CKPT_DIR = results/cl_confirmation_fixed/checkpoints/C_split_128_seed42 does not exist in the repo, so `open()` raises FileNotFoundError before any checkpoint is even considered. This is the first statement in main(), so the script cannot run at all today.
evidence: Lines 61-63; results/cl_confirmation_fixed MISSING on disk.
fix: Guard the config path with a clear existence check and actionable error (which run/seed must be present first); do not assume the results tree exists.

title: Empty-results DataFrame raises KeyError before the 'in' guard can protect it
description: If both checkpoints are missing but the config loaded (the 'only checkpoints missing' path), the loop skips every stage and results stays []. Then df = pd.DataFrame([]) has no columns, and the verdict line evaluates the ternary condition `"post_T2" in df["stage"].values` first -- df["stage"] raises KeyError: 'stage' before the membership test or the `else 0` fallback can run. So the intended empty-case fallback never fires; the script crashes.
evidence: Line 120 `df = pd.DataFrame(results)`; line 126 `... if "post_T2" in df["stage"].values else 0`. With results==[] the DataFrame has no 'stage' column.
fix: Handle the empty case before indexing: e.g. `if df.empty or "post_T2" not in df["stage"].values: post_t2_v2a = None` and branch the verdict on None (report 'no data' rather than a number).

title: Misleading 'transfer did not survive' verdict when post_T2 is simply absent
description: When df is non-empty (e.g. only post_T3 present) but has no post_T2 row, the ternary falls to `else 0`, so post_t2_v2a=0 and the code prints the failure branch: 'Transfer DID NOT survive. V2A = 0.0% (near chance).' This reports a fabricated 0.0% and a scientific conclusion for a condition that was never evaluated -- absence of data is silently rendered as a negative result.
evidence: Line 126 `else 0`; lines 134-137 print the failure verdict using post_t2_v2a.
fix: Distinguish 'not evaluated' (None) from a measured low value; only emit a verdict when post_T2 was actually scored.

title: Magic verdict thresholds >20 and >12 for V2A survival
description: The verdict tiers hardcode V2A>20 (SURVIVED) and V2A>12 (PARTIALLY) with no derivation or link to chance. Chance here is 100/num_classes = 10% (num_classes=10 at line 95), so 20 and 12 are ~2x and ~1.2x chance, but that rationale is undocumented and the constants are unnamed, making the pass/fail scientific call opaque and easy to drift.
evidence: Lines 127 `if post_t2_v2a > 20:` and 131 `elif post_t2_v2a > 12:`.
fix: Define named thresholds relative to the eval's own chance (e.g. chance = 100/num_classes; survived if V2A > chance + margin) and document the margin choice.

title: Unused imports: numpy and random_split
description: `import numpy as np` (11) and `random_split` (14) are never used in this file (grep: np. count 0; random_split count 1 = import only).
evidence: Line 11 import numpy; line 14 imports random_split; no other references.
fix: Remove the two unused imports.

title: Missing config_nmnist.json crashes main() (points at results/cl_confirmation)
description: main() opens CKPT_DIR/config_nmnist.json unconditionally (100-101). CKPT_DIR = results/cl_confirmation/checkpoints/C_split_128_seed42 (note: cl_confirmation, not cl_confirmation_fixed) does not exist, so the first line of main() raises FileNotFoundError. All three torch.load calls at 128/139-140/161 would also fail, but the config open fails first.
evidence: Lines 100-103; results/cl_confirmation MISSING on disk. CKPT_DIR defined at line 32.
fix: Guard the config and each checkpoint path with existence checks and clear errors; note the directory name differs from eval_transfer_fixed.py (cl_confirmation vs cl_confirmation_fixed) -- confirm which run this diagnostic targets.

title: Unused imports: numpy, pandas, random_split
description: numpy (14), pandas (15), and random_split (29) are imported but never used (grep: np. 0, pd. 0, random_split 1 = import only). The seed note flagged numpy/pandas as ~unused; confirmed, plus random_split.
evidence: Lines 14, 15, 29; no np./pd./random_split usage elsewhere in the file.
fix: Remove all three unused imports.

title: Magic gate-uniformity threshold 1e-6
description: all_identical is decided by (gates.std(dim=0) < 1e-6).all() with an unnamed, undocumented 1e-6 tolerance. The pass/fail of the gate-sanity check hinges on this constant; it should be a named, justified tolerance.
evidence: Line 89 `"all_identical": bool((gates.std(dim=0) < 1e-6).all()),`.
fix: Promote 1e-6 to a named constant with a one-line rationale (e.g. GATE_STD_EPS).

title: T1 accuracy reported without spike-rate/sparsity or timestep cost
description: eval_t1 (45-56) computes and the script prints T1 accuracy at post-T1/T2/T3 (130-132, 183-185) with no accompanying spike rate, sparsity, or timestep count -- the 'accuracy never travels alone' rule. Severity is low because this is a stdout diagnostic, not a persisted result or paper number, but the pattern should not be copied into result-writing code.
evidence: Lines 130-132 print `{acc:.2f}%` with no cost metric; eval_t1 returns only accuracy.
fix: If these numbers are ever surfaced beyond debugging, report mean spike rate and time_steps (25) alongside; otherwise label clearly as a debug-only accuracy.

title: Unused import: dataclasses
description: `import dataclasses` (10) is never used (grep: dataclasses. count 0). Same unused import appears in run_cl_rehearsal.py (see CLE-026).
evidence: Line 10; no dataclasses.* reference in the file.
fix: Remove the import.

title: _is_complete_result treats a header-only CSV as complete (false skip)
description: _is_complete_result checks only that all EXPECTED_COLUMNS are present as columns (58), not that any row exists. A CSV written with a header but zero data rows (or a truncated/failed prior write that still has the header) satisfies the check, so run_confirmation_cell prints 'SKIP' (186) and returns {} -- the cell is silently skipped despite having produced no result.
evidence: Line 57-58 `df = pd.read_csv(csv_path); return all(col in df.columns ...)`; line 185-187 skip logic.
fix: Also require len(df) >= 1 (and ideally that the single expected row's key fields are non-null) before treating the result as complete.

title: cfg.pin_memory and cfg.num_workers are ignored by the DataLoaders
description: Every DataLoader hardcodes num_workers=0 and omits pin_memory, so cfg.pin_memory=True (371) and cfg.num_workers=0 (371) are never actually consumed. num_workers=0 is correct on macOS/MPS, but silently ignoring config fields means the saved config.json advertises settings the run did not use (pin_memory=True in particular). Same in run_cl_rehearsal.py.
evidence: Loaders at 88-95, 120-127, 141-148 pass num_workers=0 literally and no pin_memory; grep pin_memory=cfg count 0.
fix: Either pass cfg.pin_memory (and keep num_workers=0 with a comment on the macOS constraint) or drop the unused fields from the config so provenance matches behaviour.

title: Saved config misrepresents actual training length (cfg 50/12 vs hardcoded 15/5)
description: cfg sets max_epochs=50, patience=12 (368) but every train_task call hardcodes num_epochs=15, patience=5 (226,266,302), and align uses num_epochs=5 (241). The config saved next to each checkpoint via cfg.to_json (231,271,307) and results/master_config.json (402) therefore records 50/12, not the 15/5 the run truly used. Anyone reproducing from the saved config would train 50 epochs and not reproduce the checkpoints -- a provenance/reproducibility defect. Identical pattern in run_cl_rehearsal.py (201/249/291 vs 381).
evidence: cfg max_epochs=50, patience=12 at line 368; train_task hardcodes num_epochs=15, patience=5 at 226/266/302; cfg.to_json at 231/271/307/402.
fix: Drive num_epochs/patience from cfg (add per-phase fields if 15 vs 50 is intentional) so the persisted config equals what actually ran. Apply the same fix in run_cl_rehearsal.py.

title: forgetting_T1_T3 is the incremental post-T2->post-T3 drop, not total T1 forgetting the name implies
description: forgetting_T1_T3 = acc_t1_after_t2 - acc_t1_after_t3 (327) measures only the T1 drop that occurs during T3 (between post-T2 and post-T3). The name reads as total T1->T3 forgetting, which is actually a separate column total_forgetting_T1_T3 = acc_t1_after - acc_t1_after_t3 (329). This is a real mislabel risk: a summary or paper could quote 'T1_T3 forgetting' and use the incremental value. Identical construction in run_cl_rehearsal.py:336.
evidence: Line 327 forgetting_t1_t3 = acc_t1_after_t2 - acc_t1_after_t3; line 329 total_forgetting_t1_t3 = acc_t1_after - acc_t1_after_t3.
fix: Rename to forgetting_T1_during_T3 (incremental) or make the pair unambiguous in a data dictionary; ensure downstream analysis and paper text pick the intended one. Mirror in run_cl_rehearsal.py.

title: forgetting_T2_T3 and total_forgetting_T2_T3 are computed identically (always equal)
description: forgetting_t2_t3 = acc_t2_after - acc_t2_after_t3 (328) and total_forgetting_t2_t3 = acc_t2_after - acc_t2_after_t3 (330) are the same expression, so the two CSV columns are always byte-identical -- redundant, and asymmetric with the T1 pair where the two columns genuinely differ (327 vs 329). Either total_forgetting_T2_T3 was meant to be a different quantity, or one column is superfluous. Same in run_cl_rehearsal.py:337/339.
evidence: Lines 328 and 330 are identical expressions.
fix: Drop the redundant column or, if a distinct quantity was intended (e.g. an incremental T2 measure), compute it correctly. Mirror in run_cl_rehearsal.py.

title: Dead else branch in _events_to_dense max_time guard
description: `max_time = events["t"].max() if len(events) > 0 else 1` (105) sits inside `if len(events) > 0:` (104), so the `else 1` is unreachable. Cosmetic but confusing, and copy-pasted verbatim into 4 files (see CLE-031).
evidence: Line 104 guard, line 105 redundant ternary.
fix: Drop the redundant ternary: inside the guard, `max_time = events["t"].max()`.

title: Results CSV stores accuracy/forgetting with no spike-rate/sparsity cost metric
description: The persisted result dict (332-347) carries T1/T2/T3 test accuracy, FWT and forgetting but no spike rate or sparsity; only the timestep count survives, and only indirectly via the separately saved config (time_steps=25). Per the 'accuracy never travels alone' rule, an SNN accuracy in a results CSV that downstream figures/analysis read must ship with its spike-rate/sparsity and timestep cost. Same for run_cl_rehearsal.py:341-356.
evidence: result dict keys at 332-347 contain no spike/sparsity field; time_steps only in cfg.to_json output.
fix: Add measured mean spike rate / sparsity (and time_steps) columns to the result row, or document that cost metrics live in a companion file. Mirror in run_cl_rehearsal.py.

title: Hardcoded comparison-table numbers printed to the log alongside live results
description: The COMPARISON TABLE prints live values (res[...] for C_rehearsal, xfer[...] for transfer) interleaved with HARDCODED literals for the A_no_align, C_unfrozen and C_frozen columns: e.g. 97.21/97.28/97.29/79.64/77.78/78.41/-0.08/1.86 (A_no_align), 97.50/54.85/60.09/75.09/76.28/75.38/37.41/-1.19/36.92/0.59 (C_unfrozen), 97.50/15.33/13.30/81.67/80.57/82.20/84.20/1.10/14.80/0.21 (C_frozen). These have no CSV provenance in-repo and are formatted identically to the live column, so a reader copying the table into the paper cannot distinguish measured from hardcoded. This is the 'other script writing hardcoded numbers to a log' the assignment asks to hunt -- a RULE-1 hazard even though it goes to stdout rather than a CSV.
evidence: Literal floats embedded in print f-strings at lines 435-444 (e.g. `{97.21:>14.2f}%`, `{84.20:>14.2f}%`, `{0.59:>14.4f}`).
fix: Load the comparison conditions' numbers from their own result CSVs (or omit those columns) instead of hardcoding; if a baseline CSV does not exist, print 'unsourced'/'n/a' rather than a literal.

title: Unused import: dataclasses
description: `import dataclasses` (15) is never used (grep: dataclasses. count 0). Same as run_cl_confirmation_fixed.py (CLE-017).
evidence: Line 15; no dataclasses.* reference.
fix: Remove the import.

title: Magic numbers: raw buffer size 200 (vs cfg 50), max_batches 100, drift eps 1e-6
description: RawInputReplayBuffer(samples_per_class=200) (178) hardcodes 200 while cfg.replay_samples_per_class=50 (386) governs the embedding buffer -- two different, unexplained capacities. raw_buffer.populate(..., max_batches=100) (214,275) hardcodes 100. The backbone-drift sanity uses total_l2 < 1e-6 (330) as a magic threshold. None are named or justified; they affect what rehearsal actually sees.
evidence: Line 178 samples_per_class=200; lines 214,275 max_batches=100; line 330 `if total_l2 < 1e-6`.
fix: Promote to named, documented constants or cfg fields; reconcile the 200 vs cfg's 50 so the rehearsal capacity is intentional and recorded.

title: Backbone-drift check indexes sd_t3[k] by sd_t1's keys without a membership check
description: The drift loop iterates keys of sd_t1 and computes (sd_t1[k] - sd_t3[k]).norm() (326-327) with no check that k exists in sd_t3. If the two checkpoints have different key sets (e.g. arch change between saves), this raises KeyError. Low likelihood because both come from the same model class, hence low confidence, but the sibling phase1_sanity_check.compare_state_dicts (65-66) does guard for the missing key -- an inconsistency worth aligning.
evidence: Lines 324-328; contrast phase1_sanity_check.py:65-66 which handles `k not in sd2`.
fix: Skip or record keys missing from sd_t3 (mirror compare_state_dicts) before subtracting.

title: Per-task checkpoint-skip silently loads stale weights instead of retraining
description: For each task, `if ckpt.exists(): print skip; model.load_state_dict(torch.load(ckpt))` (220-222, 260-262, 296-298) skips training whenever a matching final_{task}_{task}.pt is present. This is the documented repo trap (training silently skipped on existing checkpoint) replicated per task: a stale checkpoint from older code yields stale results that look freshly computed, with only a transient stdout note. Same in run_cl_rehearsal.py (195-197, 243-245, 285-287).
fix: Record and check a code/version/config hash against the checkpoint before skipping, or require an explicit --resume flag; at minimum warn loudly (not just print) and log the checkpoint mtime.

title: build_full_loaders and SHD/N-MNIST loader helpers are duplicated across the cluster
description: build_full_loaders (69-179) is nearly identical between run_cl_confirmation_fixed.py and run_cl_rehearsal.py (47-157). The _events_to_dense SHD-densify helper is copy-pasted into 4 files (run_cl_confirmation_fixed 101-111, run_cl_rehearsal 79-89, eval_transfer_fixed 46-56, run_rehearsal_transfer_eval_only 65-75), and build_nmnist_test_loader/build_shd_test_loader are duplicated between eval_transfer_fixed and phase1_sanity_check. Divergent edits to any copy (transform windows, split seed, densify logic) silently produce mismatched preprocessing across scripts that are supposed to be comparable.
evidence: build_full_loaders present in two files with matching bodies; _events_to_dense present in 4 files; build_*_test_loader present in eval_transfer_fixed.py:33-58 and phase1_sanity_check.py:34-42.
fix: Extract the loaders and _events_to_dense into a shared, import-safe module (alongside m7_trimodal_run_provenance) and import them; do not re-declare per script.

title: Dead else branch in _events_to_dense duplicated across four files
description: The redundant `... if len(events) > 0 else 1` inside an `if len(events) > 0:` block (dead else) recurs in eval_transfer_fixed.py:50, run_rehearsal_transfer_eval_only.py:69, run_cl_confirmation_fixed.py:105, and run_cl_rehearsal.py:83. One shared helper (CLE-030) would remove all four at once.
evidence: Line 50 (and the three siblings) `max_time = events["t"].max() if len(events) > 0 else 1` under an outer len>0 guard.
fix: Remove the dead ternary in all four copies (best done when consolidating into a shared helper).

title: ExperimentConfig literal block triplicated across the run/eval scripts
description: The same ~14-line ExperimentConfig(...) literal is declared three times: run_cl_confirmation_fixed.py (364-377), run_cl_rehearsal.py (377-390), and run_rehearsal_transfer_eval_only.py (22-35). They must stay in lockstep for the eval scripts to match the runs, but nothing enforces it (see the replay_weight drift, CLE-003).
evidence: Three near-identical ExperimentConfig literal blocks at the cited locations.
fix: Define the base config once (a factory or a JSON that all three load) and have the eval scripts read the config saved with the checkpoint rather than re-declaring it.

title: evaluate_cross_modal_transfer pulls in scikit-learn, which is absent from requirements.txt
description: run_rehearsal_transfer_eval_only.py (19), eval_transfer_fixed.py (29) and run_cl_rehearsal.py (44) import evaluate_cross_modal_transfer from utils/cross_modal_transfer.py, which imports sklearn (LogisticRegression, silhouette_score, cosine_similarity at utils/cross_modal_transfer.py:34-36). code/requirements.txt contains no scikit-learn/sklearn entry (grep count 0), so on a clean pinned environment all three scripts fail at import with ModuleNotFoundError: sklearn. This is a transitive but hard runtime break for the whole eval cluster.
evidence: Import lines 19/29/44; utils/cross_modal_transfer.py:34-36 import sklearn; code/requirements.txt has no scikit-learn.
fix: Add scikit-learn (pinned) to code/requirements.txt.
